newsitem.title: USA: Georgia indicators signal continued slow growth.
newsitem.headline: Georgia indicators signal continued slow growth.

text.p: Georgia's Composite Index of Leading Economic Indicators moved up for the seventh time in eight months in February, signalling continued economic expansion, state Labor Commissioner David Poythress said in his monthly report.
Leading indicators, designed to predict economic activity three to six months ahead, rose 1.24 points to 147 on a 1988 index base of 100.
The Composite Index of Coincident Indicators, which measures current economic conditions, rose 0.14 points to 145.22.
Both indices preceded the Federal Reserve's March 25 interest rate increase. The increase was expected to further slow Georgia's economic growth, which has dropped from pre-Olympic levels.

Poythress said February's rise in the leading indicators was mainly influenced by a sharp drop in initial unemployment claims. New claims fell 21.25 percent from January, to 25,457 in February. Continuing claims fell by 3.5 percent, to 170,839 during the month.
The state's unemplyment rate edged down to 4.6 percent in January from 4.7 percent in February.
Residential building permits dropped to 5,569 in February, down 7.47 from January and down 26.4 percent over last February.
Total nonfarm employment rose less than one-tenth of a percent to 3.58 million in February, an increase of 2.9 percent over the year.

The average manufacturing workweek decreased by 18 minutes in February to 42.3 hours. Average weekly manufacturing earnings also declined 0.3 percent in February to $485.12, but that was 4.8 percent higher than a year ago.
The state granted 35,674 new motor vehicle titles in February, down 50 from January.

State revenue collections increased to $860.8 million, up 1.1 percent from January and up 3.3 percent from last year. Sales tax collections, which have slowed since the October decrease in sales taxes on groceries, rose to $341.4 million in February, an increaes of 2.66 percent over January but down 6.6 percent over last year.
